context.title: Jacob Flees from Laban
context.summary: Told by God to return home, Jacob slips away with his family and flocks; Rachel steals her father's household idols, Laban pursues, and the two men end with a covenant of stones at Mizpah.
context.background: Laban overtakes Jacob in Gilead, east of the Jordan. Jacob complains that over twenty years Laban changed his wages ten times (v. 41). The heap is named in two languages, Aramaic Jegar-sahadutha and Hebrew Galeed, both meaning heap of witness (v. 47).

customs.note: Small household idols, probably tied to family protection or worship; whether they also signaled inheritance rights is debated. Rachel hides them by sitting on them.

watchFor: God is called 'the fear of Isaac' (vv. 42, 53).
The 'Mizpah' words (v. 49) were originally a wary truce: each man asks God to watch the other.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Laban
people.summary: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24).

people.name: Rachel
people.summary: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28).

people.name: Leah
people.summary: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel (Gen. 29:16). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father (Gen. 29:23). She was “tender-eyed” (17).

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32).

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: Paddan-aram
places.summary: The plain of Aram, or the plain of the highlands, (Gen. 25:20; 28:2, 5-7; 31:18, etc.), commonly regarded as the district of Mesopotamia lying around Haran.

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” (Gen. 31:25).

places.name: Galeed
places.summary: Heap of witness, the name of the pile of stones erected by Jacob and Laban to mark the league of friendship into which they entered with each other (Gen. 31:47, 48).

places.name: Jegar-sahadutha
places.summary: Pile of testimony, the Aramaic or Syriac name which Laban gave to the pile of stones erected as a memorial of the covenant between him and Jacob (Gen. 31:47), who, however, called it in Hebrew by an equivalent name, Galeed.

places.name: Mizpah
places.summary: A place in Gilead, so named by Laban, who overtook Jacob at this spot (Gen. 31:49) on his return to Palestine from Padan-aram. Here Jacob and Laban set up their memorial cairn of stones.
